newsitem.title: UK: Canada bonds lead way in week,Italy skids -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds lead way in week,Italy skids -Salomon.

text.p: Canadian government bonds were the top performing market in the week ended February 13 while a shaky Italian market registered the worst losses, according to Salomon Brothers data on Friday.
Canadian bonds notched up a 1.20 percent return in the week and were up 0.81 percent in U.S. dollar terms at a time when the U.S. currency made advances against most major currencies.

Canadian dealers said the domestic bond market was encouraged by strength in U.S. Treasuries but outperformed their neighbours who were swamped with supply. There was also some optimism ahead of a federal Canadian budget next week.

Swiss bonds came in second with a 1.13 percent return in Swiss francs, while third-placed British gilts returned 0.99 percent in sterling. Italian BTPs were the only market in the main Salomons government bond index to show a loss in local currency terms, with investors losing 0.10 percent in the week. In dollar terms, Italian debt showed a 2.24 percent loss.
Concerns about Italy's fiscal situation and residual worries about its progress towards European monetary union weighed on Italian debt, analysts said.
The overall Salomon index was up 0.56 percent in local currencies and down 0.43 in dollar terms.

After Canada's robust performance, the only other markets to make gains for dollar-based investors were U.S. Treasuries with a 0.69 percent return, Britain with 0.39 percent and Sweden with 0.31 percent.

Except for Italy, most European bond markets turned in decent performances. Dutch debt returned 0.84 percent in the local currency, France and Denmark made 0.76 percent gains, Sweden made 0.73 percent, Belgium 0.71 percent, Spain 0.59 percent and German Bunds 0.58. Japanese government bonds turned in a relatively weak performance, showing a modest 0.11 percent return in yen and a 0.79 percent loss in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
